q: From a point on the ground, the angle of elevation of the top of a tower is 45°. If the tower is 20 m high, how far is the point from the base of the tower?
exp: tan 45° = height/base; 1 = 20/base; base = 20 m. Answer: 20 m

From the top of a 60 m high building, the angle of elevation of the top of a tower is 30° and the angle of depression of its foot is 45°. What is the height of the tower?
exp: Distance from building = 60/tan 45° = 60 m. Tower height above building = 60 tan 30° = 60/√3 = 20√3 m. Total height = 60 + 20√3 = 20(3 + √3) m. Answer: 20(3 + √3) m

q: A man standing at a point observes the top of a tower at an angle of elevation of 30°. He walks 40 m towards the tower and now observes the top at 60°. What is the height of the tower?
The angle of elevation of a cloud from a point 60 m above a lake is 30° and the angle of depression of its reflection in the lake is 60°. What is the height of the cloud above the lake?
exp: Let cloud height above lake = h; height above point = h - 60; horizontal distance x = (h-60)/tan30° = (h-60)√3. Reflection is at depth h below lake, so h+60 below point: tan60° = (h+60)/x; √3 = (h+60)/((h-60)√3); 3(h-60) = h+60; 3h - 180 = h + 60; 2h = 240; h = 120 m. Answer: 120 m
